{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study is a review of animal models for ASD, but it does not report a quantitative measure of agreement between animal model results and human clinical outcomes. It discusses the strengths and weaknesses of various models but does not provide concordance rates or translation statistics.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "Here we review the genetic and environmental risk factors for ASD and how those are modeled in animals as well as hPSC-derived 2D and 3D models. We highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each model and advocate for orthogonal validation across different model systems...",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "neurodegeneration",
    "psychiatric"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Autism spectrum disorder (ASD), characterized by restricted, repetitive behavior and interests as well as impairment in social communication and adaptive difficulties, is an NDD affecting around 1–3% of individuals globally...",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "A variety of animals have been used to model ASD phenotypes [169, 176, 184, 185, 186, 187, 188, 189, 190, 191, 192, 193], of which mice, rats, pigs, and non-human primates are discussed below.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "pig",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "A variety of animals have been used to model ASD phenotypes [169, 176, 184, 185, 186, 187, 188, 189, 190, 191, 192, 193], of which mice, rats, pigs, and non-human primates are discussed below.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Common behavioral tests employed for the evaluation of ASD-like behaviors in mice include the three-chambered assay for sociability, ultrasonic vocalization for communication, marble burying for stereotypy, and the T-maze or Morris water maze for spatial memory as well as cognitive flexibility [177, 178]."
